g: Supposing that, assuming that, in the circumstances that; suppositive used to introduce a condition that may be (or prove to be) either true or false.
I'll do it next week if I have time.
(computing) A keyword that invokes conditional processing: in the event that a given condition is true, execute the given statement(s) (otherwise execute other statements).
if A then B else C
Supposing that; used with past or past perfect subjunctive to indicate a counterfactual or hypothetical condition.
If she hadn't told me, I wouldn't know.
(usually hyperbolic) Even if; even in the circumstances that.
I wouldn't marry you if you were the last man on earth.
Considering the fact that; given that; introducing a condition that is known to be true.
The drain's blocked — and if the drain's blocked, the water won't flow.
(informal) An uncertainty, possibility, condition, doubt etc.
The board can't approve this project; there are too many ifs.
If none of someone's attempts or plans succeed.
(logic, mathematics) Is equivalent to; implies and is implied by; is true and false in the same cases as.
A rectangle is a square if and only if all four of its sides have the same length.
(by extension, informal) Synonym of if (with added intensity)
I'll let you go to the concert if and only if you clean your room.
At the time of an event, contingent on that event happening at all.
(idiomatic) Used to suggest or state tentatively that something may be the case (often the opposite of something previously implied).
The situation is, if anything, worsening rather than improving.
(idiomatic) Used in questions when the speaker does not know for sure if the listener will have an answer.
What can you tell me, if anything, about this book?
If that condition is met; if the situation presents itself; in the event of the case happening; when circumstances so require.
(grammar) A type of dependent clause that expresses a condition and its potential result.
If at any time; if at all.
I seldom if ever travel abroad.
Used to emphasize the truth of a characterization.
He's a plagiarist if ever there was one.
Synonym of if ever there was one.
There's a messed-up face if I ever saw one.

Without any following verb, implies a request to interrupt, to speak at length, or to take control, often when the speaker can introduce new, unexpected information or, alternatively, when the speaker disapproves of how a task was done and proposes to redo it.
Used to soften the effect of a statement that is self-aggrandizing or is embarrassing to the listener.
A phrase said to introduce advice, i.e. to express what one would do in the interlocutor's situation.
Used before stating something that the speaker believes to be correct
Observes, with (sometimes ironic) surprise, that a specified thing or person is present.
Why, if it isn't Bill! Come on in, Bill!
(colloquial) Regardless of how much effort or struggle is required from one.
I'm going to pass this exam if it kills me!
If a certain condition were not met; used to indicate that a particular person, event, etc. prevented a certain outcome.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see if, it, you, please.
(idiomatic) If it makes no difference; if nobody minds; if it doesn't bother anyone.
If it's all the same to you, I'd prefer to stay at a hotel instead of at your house.
Used to characterize a look of strong hostility.
If I have correctly remembered the details.
(gambling) A type of money collected from earnings on one race which is then automatically applied to a subsequent race in the case when an if-bet is placed.
(idiomatic) If necessary; if there is a need.
(idiomatic) If need be; if there is a need.
(plain literal sense) Indicates that a statement is true in the event that a condition is not satisfied.
The plant will die if not watered.
Indicates that one statement at least is true, and possibly a second, stronger statement is true; perhaps even.
He did as well as expected, if not better.
Indicates that one statement is true, but a second is not; but not.
I saw that he had improved his manners if not his scruffy appearance.
If (something) were not (or had not been) there; in the absence of (something); without.
If not for her surgical skill, you'd be dead now, so some appreciation may be in order.
(idiomatic) At the very least; as a minimum.
He must be fifty if he's a day.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see if, only.
It made me feel better, if only for a moment.
(idiomatic) I wish that; would (that) (archaic). Signifies a wish or desire for the present or the future.
If only I could win the lottery.
(idiomatic) I wish that; would (that) (archaic). Signifies a regret about an action in the past.
If only I had listened to my parents.
(idiomatic) Even if for no other reason than; only just.
I was pretty sure what I wanted, but I still tried on another if only to make sure.
(idiomatic) Signifies a hypothetical or wishful precondition, or one which would be simple but is nonetheless unlikely, for a hypothetical, counterfactual, or future outcome.
He could be a great student if only he got [or: if he only got] a little non-judgmental encouragement.
(chiefly sarcastic) If only somebody at the top of an abusive hierarchy were aware of the abuses, they would take action to stop them.
Contingent upon the possibility or convenience of the request.
Are you free? If so, let's go out for a meal tonight. If not, then it'll be Sat.
My car is so old that, if I were to sell it, I would get a hundred pounds, if that.
Synonym of don't that beat all.
Synonym of don't that beat all.
Expresses that something is obviously a genuine instance of something else.
Well if that's not the cutest McDonald's I've seen in my lifeǃ
(idiomatic) Used to denote a location with an interesting or controversial history.
(informal) Used to introduce one's opinion, without being asked for it.
Please, kindly; used in giving a non-concrete instruction.
But imagine, if you like, a world where climate change did not exist.
So to speak, like; used to indicate that a description is not standard.
This band's genre can be described as, if you like, New Wave or Post-Punk.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see if, you, please.
(colloquial, dismissive) Used to convey lack of agreement together with a refusal to enter into or continue an argument.
Please, kindly; used in giving a non-concrete instruction.
But imagine, if you will, a world where these logistical problems were solved.
So to speak, like; used to indicate that a description is not standard.
These are "partial artifacts", if you will: the imaging process has merely amplified flaws that were already present in the original.
Used in conceding a description or choice of terms.
He wasn't a very honest person; a liar, if you will.
(chiefly Southern US, South Midland US, and some dialects in UK) If.
(gambling) A type of bet placed with a bookmaker wherein the bettor has money on a horse in a subsequent race under the condition that his horse in an earlier race also wins.

(US, politics, of a speech, etc.) That equivocates on an issue while appearing to affirm both sides, by asserting that each is correct depending on which of two stated alternatives is used as the definition of a key term.
A proposition or statement about what should or does occur when a certain condition is met.
(programming) A conditional statement; a line of code that specifies a Boolean condition to check and a statement to execute when that Boolean evaluates to true.
(programming) A statement that executes different code based on whether a condition is true or false.
(mathematics) The doctrine that all mathematical statements are conditional in form, meaning they can be expressed in the form "p implies q", (i.e. if p then q).
A complex system of divination in Yoruba religion.
Any soft coral of the family Ifalukellidae
(computing, programming) A construct in source code that allows another part of the code to run only if a specified identifier is defined in the program.
(pharmacology) A selective inhibitor of the NMDA receptor.
A potent and selective thromboxane receptor antagonist.
The state or quality of being iffy.
(slang) Of dubious authenticity, legitimacy or legality.
He's selling new CD players for £20 each – that sounds a bit iffy to me.
The weather is still iffy for Saturday's rocket launch.
A Philippine and Pacific island tree (Intsia bijuga), yielding a valuable brown dye and having a very hard and durable dark wood.
A Zambian stew made from vegetables and ground peanuts.
Any of the genus Iflavirus of RNA viruses that infect various insects.
(pharmacology) A particular drug used in chemotherapy.
A non-apology of the form "I'm sorry if you were upset" or "I'm sorry if you took it that way".
For quotations using this term, see Citations:ifpology.
(Internet) A section of a web page that can act as the container for a second separate page or resource.
(Islam) A kind of djinn mentioned in the Qur'an.
(Arab mythology) A demon, evil spirit, often associated with the underworld.
A species of passerine bird endemic to New Guinea, in full the blue-capped ifrit.
A blue-capped ifrita, a bird, native to New Guinea, of species Ifrita kowaldi, sole species of its genus and family.
hypotheticals; counterfactuals; things that one only wishes were the case
Conditions, limitations or qualifications placed on something.
I'm not happy with this contract. There are too many ifs and buts.
(Islam) The evening meal that breaks each day's fast during Ramadan, traditionally beginning with dates and water.
Iftars can be social events, where people congregate to eat and socialize.
